Velika Gorica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Velika Gorica, Croatia

Not demolished. Velika Gorica's small Jewish community numbered 67 people in 1921, declining to 37 by 1931. Its most notable member was Filip Deutsch (1828–1919), a nobleman and industrialist whose company produced the columns for the town's local bridge in 1884; in 1911, he founded a steam sawmill that at its peak employed about 600 workers, offering unusually progressive conditions for the era — eight-hour workdays, hot meals, a decent salary, and housing. This cemetery, built in the 19th century, still holds a few surviving tombstones, ranging from 1906 to 1938.
